transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-11-13
- Time: 15:00 PST
- Duration: ~54 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen, Rafael Ortiz (Redwood); Priya Nair, Ben Holloway, Lena Ortiz, Tom Wu (Stageline)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on onboarding plan, infra requirements for a 6-week pilot, SSO/compliance checklist, and a scheduling of a technical deep-dive to scope VPC/private deployment options. Some discussion around dedicated vs hosted, latency objectives, and data retention.

Topics covered:
- Pilot goals and success metrics
- Network & VPC requirements
- Authentication/SSO and audit logging
- Model variants / latency vs cost trade-offs
- Observability and runbook handoff

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll kick it off, I'm Maya, AE on the account, Rafael my SE will go over the tech bits. How's everyone?
[00:12] Priya Nair: Hi Maya, thanks — excited to get started. We've got a few people from platform and security.
[00:18] Rafael Ortiz: Hey, good to meet you all. I'll try to keep the deep dive high level today and then we can schedule the full infra session.
[00:27] Ben Holloway: Sounds good. We're mainly here to figure out what we need to prep for a pilot and what the network + compliance ask will look like.
[00:35] Maya Chen: Great. Quick agenda — walk through the pilot goals, timeline, infra needs, SSO and SOC2 materials, then Rafael will talk about routing, caching, and batching. We'll finish with next steps.
[00:46] Tom Wu: One ask up front — we need to hit p95 latency under 300ms for our customer-facing flows. Is that achievable on-hosted?
[00:54] Rafael Ortiz: Short answer: depends. For short prompts, hosted with the smaller LLM variants generally hit <200ms p95. If you have long seqs or heavy concurrency, sometimes Dedicated with pinned capacity is easier to guarantee. Also caching and KV cache pre-warm help a lot.
[01:10] Priya Nair: Our workload is mixed — some short lookup prompts, some 1k token summarizations. We'll share distributions.
[01:18] Ben Holloway: And we run a lot of batched jobs overnight for embeddings — cost matters there.
[01:25] Rafael Ortiz: Right — embeddings batch jobs are classic candidate for Dedicated or a hybrid: hosted for live, dedicated for batch. The platform has policies to route by latency vs cost.
[01:36] Lena Ortiz: On security, we need to understand what logs you keep, encryption at rest, and whether we can bring our own KMS. Also SSO — we need SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
[01:47] Maya Chen: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning, and BYOK via KMS integrations for private deployments. We can share the SOC2 pack and architecture diagrams.
[01:56] Priya Nair: Good — also data residency. We're US-only but will need audit logs stored for 12 months.
[02:04] Rafael Ortiz: Audit logs can be configured for retention; for private you can push logs to your own SIEM via forwarders. For hosted we keep standard audit events and can export them on schedule.
[02:15] Tom Wu: Can you walk us through the typical onboarding runbook? What's the first week look like?
[02:22] Maya Chen: Week one: account setup, API keys, SSO, basic routes + credentials. Week two: infra deep-dive, vetting VPC peering or private connectors. Week three: pilot model selection, test prompts, run benchmarks. Week four to six: pilot analytics, tweak batching/quantization, go/no-go.
[02:36] Ben Holloway: For VPC — do you require peering or is a connector ok? We run strict network policies.
[02:42] Rafael Ortiz: Both are supported. VPC peering is common for private deployments; for hosted we have a secure connector pattern that uses mutual TLS and restricted ingress. We'll capture Ben's firewall rules we need.
[02:55] Priya Nair: We might start with hosted + connector to move faster, then migrate to private later. Is there any lock-in risk?
[03:02] Rafael Ortiz: No lock-in. The API is stable, and you can pin model versions or export workloads. The main diffs are control plane access and network setup.
[03:10] Tom Wu: About cost estimates — can you give a rough for a pilot with say 50k tokens/day interactive and 500k tokens batch embedding per week?
[03:19] Maya Chen: We can run numbers — I'll send a pricing worksheet after this. There's per-token pricing for hosted, and reserved capacity tiers for Dedicated which lower unit cost for batch.
[03:29] Ben Holloway: Please include quantization options in that estimate — we might accept slightly lower quality for big cost savings.
[03:34] Rafael Ortiz: We'll include typical quant profiles and perf tradeoffs. Quantized int8 or 4-bit can cut GPU memory and cost significantly, but affects output slightly for generative tasks. We'll recommend by workload.
[03:48] Maya Chen: Rafael, can you give a quick overview of caching and batching features — Ben asked about large embedding runs.
[03:55] Rafael Ortiz: Sure — we do automatic prefix caching and KV cache for chat. For embeddings, continuous batching is available where we accumulate until a threshold or timeout. You can set your batch window. Also we support memoization layer for repeat prompts which saves tokens/cost.
[04:12] Ben Holloway: How do we measure quality regressions if we change models or quantize? We need guardrails.
[04:19] Rafael Ortiz: Good question — our Optimize toolkit ties evaluations to prompt sets. You can register a validation set and run regression alerts when metrics deviate. We'll help set that up for the pilot.
[04:30] Lena Ortiz: For compliance, do you provide audit trails per request? We need request-level traceability for certain endpoints.
[04:37] Rafael Ortiz: We can provide request IDs, timestamps, user tokens and model version in logs. For private deployments you can push full logs to your own SIEM.
[04:46] Tom Wu: On monitoring, what's in Redwood Console? Can my devs see per-route latency and token costs?
[04:53] Maya Chen: Yes — Console shows token-level cost, per-route latency breakdown, per-model dashboards, traces and error rates. You can create alerts for regressions.
[05:03] Priya Nair: Ok, let's talk pilot success criteria — our product team wants p95 < 300ms for customer flows, embeddings throughput of X per hour, and integration with our SSO.
[05:13] Maya Chen: Sounds good. We'll codify those into the pilot plan. Any blockers on timeline? When do you want to start?
[05:19] Priya Nair: As soon as possible — aiming to kick off next Monday and have pilot running within two weeks.
[05:24] Maya Chen: We can do that. Rafael, we'll need you for the infra call Monday.
[05:29] Rafael Ortiz: Yep, I'll be there. Ben, can you share node sizes and typical seq lengths? That helps model selection.
[05:36] Ben Holloway: I'll pull that after this call.
[05:40] [07:00] break in transcript noise — cross talk and brief hold music
[07:15] Rafael Ortiz: Back to routing — we recommend policy: live traffic to smaller low-latency variants, fallback to cheaper or higher-latency for batch or retries. There's also auto-fallback if a region is degraded.
[07:30] Tom Wu: If we go private, how does deployment lifecycle work? Can we do canary rollouts?
[07:37] Rafael Ortiz: Yes, our Dedicated and Private control planes support canaries, A/B and automatic fallback policies. You can pin model versions per route.
[07:47] Priya Nair: Do you have a reference infra template for AWS accounts? We want the IaC we can copy.
[07:53] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll share terraform snippets and sample cloud formation. That's in the runbook we send.
[08:01] Ben Holloway: On SSO provisioning — we use Okta. Any gotchas?
[08:06] Maya Chen: Okta + SAML + SCIM are common. We'll provide metadata and the attributes we expect.
[08:13] Lena Ortiz: One more security question — data retention on logs, and is there a way to mask PII before logs are stored?
[08:20] Rafael Ortiz: You can configure log redaction or use client-side masking. For hosted, we can also scrub or not persist payloads if needed for certain endpoints. We should map the exact events you need.
[08:33] Tom Wu: For the pilot, we want the hosted path initially but with strict logging rules.
[08:38] Maya Chen: That's doable. We'll itemize those options in the runbook.
[08:44] Priya Nair: Can Rafael talk about load testing? We want to simulate 200 concurrent users hitting the chat endpoint.
[08:51] Rafael Ortiz: We'll provide a simple k6 script or a load harness you can run. For p95 numbers, make sure your sequences and concurrency map to expected traffic; caching will change the shape substantially.
[09:03] Ben Holloway: Also can you share typical warmup strategies for KV caches?
[09:09] Rafael Ortiz: Pre-warm by replaying recent sessions or seeding with high frequency prompts. For long-form summaries, KV cache hits are less common, but prefix caching helps for repeated system prompts.
[09:21] [10:30] Maya Chen: We're close to half an hour in — wanted to check any unanswered legal/compliance blockers?
[10:35] Lena Ortiz: We need the SOC2 and encryption docs. Also a data processing addendum for the pilot.
[10:41] Maya Chen: We'll send SOC2 and a DPA template. Legal can sign a pilot DPA.
[10:46] Priya Nair: Who will be our main Redwood contact during pilot?
[10:50] Maya Chen: I'll be your customer success lead; Rafael will be tech; you can also reach out to our support SREs for 24/7 issues.
[10:58] Tom Wu: Great. Any sample telemetry we'll get during pilot?
[11:02] Rafael Ortiz: You'll have Console access with per-route metrics, traces and token breakdown and we can add custom logs.
[11:10] Ben Holloway: For the embeddings batch — do you support sharded batching across GPUs?
[11:16] Rafael Ortiz: Yes on Dedicated we can shard across a GPU pool for throughput. For hosted, batching is more single-node but autoscaling can handle volume though not as cost-efficient.
[11:29] [15:00] time jump in transcript, minor stutters
[15:05] Priya Nair: Ok let's align on dates — Maya you said you'd send runbook by Monday?
[15:11] Maya Chen: I'll send the runbook and pricing worksheet by Monday EOD West coast (due: 2025-11-17). We'll also propose times for the infra deep-dive.
[15:18] Ben Holloway: Rafael, let's do the infra deep-dive Tuesday or Wednesday if possible.
[15:22] Rafael Ortiz: Tuesday 11/18 10am PT works from my side; I'll tentatively block it.
[15:29] Lena Ortiz: Legal will review the DPA; I'll follow up with any questions.
[15:34] Tom Wu: Last question — are there any major gotchas you see in our plan?
[15:39] Rafael Ortiz: Nothing blocking from what you described — the two things to watch: sequencing long tokens will increase latency and cost (we can quantify), and network setup can add lead time if you require peering.
[15:50] Maya Chen: Perfect. I'll capture action items. Recap: Redwood sends runbook + pricing + SOC2 + IaC templates; Rafael schedules infra dive and Ben shares node/seq data; Lena reviews DPA.
[16:03] Priya Nair: That works. Thanks everyone.
[16:07] Maya Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.
[16:12] [End of recording - 54:00]
